title: Start at the epicenter
coreMove: Find the part you cannot remove without destroying what you sell, build that first, and let napkins-and-relish details wait until the center actually holds.

exampleSpecs.audience: makers tempted to polish accessories first
exampleSpecs.stakes: build the grill or build the branding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist applies the removal test to find the epicenter

exampleSpecs.audience: product teams drowning in possible tasks
exampleSpecs.stakes: ship the structural screen or the optional polish
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates structural tasks from optional edges

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who mistake motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep polishing edges or face the unbuilt core
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees that finished edge tasks are not progress on the offer

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who over-correct into bare-core minimalism
exampleSpecs.stakes: ship a core-only product forever or wrap it once it holds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist separates core-first sequence from permanent neglect of details

exampleSpecs.audience: founders who confuse spent effort with structural necessity
exampleSpecs.stakes: crown the costly feature or the non-removable one as the core
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist corrects an epicenter chosen by effort instead of removal

exampleSpecs.audience: teams building refinements in parallel with the core
exampleSpecs.stakes: build the surrounding experience now or after the center holds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist predicts the ordering cost of refining before the core works
